entries.knownHazards: Avoid with other hormonal drugs. Avoid during pregnancy and lactation. Take with food. Rare adverse effects include: mild headache and gastrointestinal symptoms. May decrease libido in males. Possible back pain and blood pressure increase [301].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Nevartoti kartu su hormoniniais vaistais, nėštumo ir žindymo metu; vartoti su maistu. Retai pasireiškia lengvas galvos skausmas, virškinimo sutrikimai, sumažėjęs libido, nugaros skausmas ar padidėjęs kraujospūdis.

entries.knownHazards: The fruit contains low concentrations of saponins[101]. Although toxic, these substances are very poorly absorbed by the body and so tend to pass through without causing harm. They are also broken down by thorough cooking. Saponins are found in many plants, including several that are often used for food, such as certain beans. It is advisable not to eat large quantities of food that contain saponins. Saponins are much more toxic to some creatures, such as fish, and hunting tribes have traditionally put large quantities of them in streams, lakes etc in order to stupefy or kill the fish[K].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Vaisiuose yra nedidelė saponinų koncentracija; šios medžiagos menkai absorbuojamos ir paprastai nekenkia, termiškai apdorojant jos sunaikinamos. Saponinai žymiai toksiškesni žuvims nei žmonėms.

entries.knownHazards: When grown on nitrogen rich soils, especially those that have been fed with chemical fertilizers, this plant can concentrate nitrates in the leaves. Nitrates are implicated in stomach cancers. Diabetics should monitor blood glucose when using. Avoid if decompensated liver cirrhosis. Possible headaches, nausea, irritability and minor gastrointestinal upset [301].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Augalas, augintas azotu turtingoje dirvoje, kaupia nitratus lapuose, kurie siejami su skrandžio vėžiu. Diabetikams rekomenduojama stebėti gliukozės kiekį kraujyje; nevartoti esant dekompensatai kepenų cirozei; galimi galvos skausmai, pykinimas ir virškinimo sutrikimai.

entries.knownHazards: Because greenleaf five-eyes belongs to the nightshade family and contains solanine-like compounds, all berries should be considered potentially toxic. Consumption may cause digestive upset or more serious symptoms in sensitive individuals. The berries' unpleasant flavour provides a natural deterrent, but foragers should avoid experimenting with them. No traditional processing techniques are known that render the berries safe or palatable, and no part of the plant should be considered reliable food.

entries.knownHazards: The leaves and the flowers contain the toxin hydrogen cyanide[240]. Some foods, notably almonds, contain small amounts of hydrogen cyanide. In small quantities, hydrogen cyanide has been shown to stimulate respiration and improve digestion, it is also claimed to be of benefit in the treatment of cancer. In excess, however, it can cause respiratory failure and even death.
